problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=2-3{t}^{2}$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=4\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=1\,\text{s}$, find the velocity (in $\text{m/s}$) of the particle at time $t.$

feedback.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{ft}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=3{t}^{2}-2t-3$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=6\,\text{ft}/\text{s}$ when $t=3\,\text{s}$, find the velocity (in $\text{ft/s}$)  of the particle at time $t.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (3{t}^{2}-2t-3)\text{d} \\  & ={t}^{3}-{t}^{2}-3t+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(3)=6.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}6 & =(3)^{3}-(3)^{2}-3(3)+C \\ 6 & =27-9-9+C \\ C & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)={t}^{3}-{t}^{2}-3t-3.$
